title: RTNC workers’ sit-in at the Primature over government pay commitments
organizer: RTNC agents and managers; national union delegation
summary: Radio Okapi reports a sit-in on 7 Nov over unpaid bonus supplements, government commitments, and social-security contributions; no participant count.

occurrence.evidence: Body and dated photo confirm a sit-in on 7 Nov.

location.evidence: Outside the Prime Minister’s office in Kinshasa.

demand.evidence: Unpaid bonus complements and government commitments; CNSS contribution transparency.

state_target.evidence: Employees addressed the government/Prime Minister’s office.

notes: The source says cabinet officials met the union delegation but no expected result followed; this is not a coded accommodation. No crowd count.
open_questions: How many workers participated simultaneously in the 7 November sit-in at the Primature?
Is any body evidence available about the sit-in’s duration or the government’s response to the salary/bonus demands?

title: Sursaut National march opposing constitutional change at avenue Kasa-Vubu/Bongolo
location: Kinshasa; avenue Kasa-Vubu toward avenue Bongolo
summary: Congo Inter reports an actual opposition march against constitutional revision, police tear gas/dispersal and detention of two leaders. It says “une cinquantaine” attended, an approximate count that does not establish a floor of 50.

occurrence.evidence: Article confirms march in Kinshasa on 14 Nov.

attendance_simultaneous.evidence: “Une cinquantaine” is approximate; no exact count or min/max.

state_target.evidence: President’s proposed constitutional change and parliamentarians addressed.

notes: The article reports two leaders detained and mistreated; it does not establish that all attendees exceeded 50. Later 27 Nov march is linked to the same broad campaign but treated as a distinct gathering.
open_questions: Does any source establish that at least 50 people attended simultaneously, rather than the approximate “une cinquantaine” wording?
Is the estimate independently corroborated, and what documented state response or consequence followed the march?

title: Sursaut National mobilization at Ngaba stopped by police
location: Rond-point Ngaba and avenue de l’Université, Kinshasa
organizer: Sursaut National / opposition and civil-society actors
summary: Actualité.cd and 7sur7 describe mobilization against constitutional change at Ngaba on 27 Nov; police stopped/dispersed the planned march. Neither body supplies attendance.

occurrence.evidence: Both bodies confirm actual mobilization at Ngaba and police intervention on 27 Nov.

location.evidence: Rond-point Ngaba; mobilization along avenue de l’Université.

state_target.evidence: Demand was directed to the national constitutional process and government.

notes: The plan was to march, but the sources indicate police stopped the march; actual mobilization occurred. Reported independence between the two outlets is not established.
open_questions: How many people were present simultaneously at the 27 November Ngaba mobilization before police stopped it?
Are the Actualite.cd and 7sur7 reports independent, and is this a separate gathering from the 14 November march despite the shared campaign?
